items.name: Brisk Walk
items.summary: The simplest sustainable activity for weight management — no equipment, no gym.
steps: Walk at a pace that raises your heart rate but still lets you hold a conversation.
Keep shoulders relaxed and stride natural.
Start with 15–20 minutes and build toward 30 or more.
tips: Split it into three 10-minute walks if that fits your day better.
Wear supportive footwear.

items.name: 10-Minute Post-Meal Walk
items.summary: A short, gentle walk after eating supports digestion and daily activity.
steps: Wait 5–10 minutes after finishing your meal.
Walk at an easy, comfortable pace for about 10 minutes.
Stay upright and breathe naturally.
tips: Try it after dinner first — it also builds an evening routine.

items.name: March in Place
items.summary: Low-impact movement for busy days — do it at home or between work calls.
steps: Stand tall and march, lifting knees to a comfortable height.
Swing your arms naturally.
Gradually increase speed or knee height as you warm up.
tips: Great as a warm-up or a desk-break habit.

items.name: Bodyweight Squat
items.summary: Builds lower-body strength, which supports metabolism and everyday movement.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Push hips back and lower as if sitting into a chair.
Press through your whole foot to stand, squeezing your glutes.
tips: Keep knees tracking over toes.
Hold a chair for support if needed.

items.name: Glute Bridge
items.summary: A gentle, back-friendly way to strengthen glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat hip-width apart.
Press through heels and lift hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a line.
Squeeze glutes, then lower slowly.
tips: Avoid arching your lower back.

items.name: Wall Push-Up
items.summary: Tones arms, chest and shoulders with almost no strain.
steps: Stand an arm's length from a wall, hands on it at shoulder height.
Bend elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
Press back to start, body in a straight line.
tips: Step feet further back to make it harder.

items.name: Dead Bug
items.summary: A spine-safe core exercise that improves posture and stability.
steps: Lie on your back, arms up, knees bent over hips.
Gently press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend opposite arm and leg, then switch.
tips: Shorten the range if your back arches.

items.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
items.summary: A mobility flow that eases stiffness and calms the mind.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Inhale: drop belly, lift chest and tailbone.
Exhale: round your spine toward the ceiling.
Move slowly with your breath.
tips: Ideal first thing in the morning or after long sitting.

items.name: Banded Lateral Walk
items.summary: Activates hips and glutes for better lower-body tone and balance.
steps: Place a loop band just above your knees.
Sit into a quarter squat.
Step sideways with tension on the band, then return.
tips: Keep toes forward and avoid leaning.

items.name: Interval Walk
items.summary: Alternating brisk and easy pace for efficient calorie burn without high impact.
steps: Warm up with 3–5 minutes of easy walking.
Walk briskly for 2 minutes, then easy for 2 minutes.
Repeat 5 times, then cool down for 3–5 minutes.
tips: Brisk means breathing harder but still able to speak in short sentences.

items.name: Goblet Squat
items.summary: A loaded squat that builds lean muscle to support body composition goals.
steps: Hold one dumbbell (or a filled water bottle) at chest height.
Sit down between your knees, chest up.
Drive up through your feet to stand.
tips: Choose a weight that makes the last 2 reps challenging, not sloppy.

items.name: The Plate Method
items.summary: A simple way to portion meals without counting calories.
steps: Fill half your plate with vegetables or salad.
Fill one quarter with protein (dal, eggs, paneer, fish, chicken).
Fill one quarter with whole-grain carbohydrates (roti, brown rice, millets).
Add a small portion of healthy fat and drink water with the meal.
tips: Works for Indian thalis, bowls and takeaway meals alike.
Adjust portions with your doctor if you have a medical condition.

items.name: Protein at Every Meal
items.summary: Helps you feel fuller for longer and supports muscle while you slim down.
steps: Choose a protein source for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Examples: eggs, curd, paneer, sprouts, dal, tofu, lean meat or fish.
Add a protein-rich snack if you're often hungry between meals.
tips: Spread protein through the day rather than one big portion.
items.note: Needs vary with kidney or other health conditions — confirm your target with your doctor.

items.name: Mindful Eating
items.frequency: At least one meal a day
items.summary: Slowing down helps you recognise fullness and avoid overeating.
steps: Sit at a table, away from screens.
Take smaller bites and put your spoon down between them.
Aim to take about 20 minutes over the meal.
Pause halfway and ask: am I still hungry?
tips: Start with just one meal a day.

items.name: Daily Hydration Routine
items.summary: Steady hydration supports energy, appetite awareness and healthy-looking skin.
steps: Start the day with a glass of water.
Keep a bottle within sight and sip regularly.
Have a glass before each main meal.
Check your urine colour — pale yellow is a good guide.
tips: Herbal tea or infused water counts too.
items.note: If you've been advised to limit fluids, follow your doctor's guidance.

items.name: Smart Snack Swaps
items.summary: Small swaps that cut empty calories without feeling restrictive.
steps: Swap sugary drinks for water, buttermilk or lemon water.
Choose roasted chana, fruit, nuts or curd over biscuits and fried snacks.
Portion snacks into a bowl rather than eating from the packet.
tips: Keep healthy options visible and treats out of sight.

items.name: Wind-Down Sleep Routine
items.summary: Quality sleep supports appetite control, mood and skin recovery.
steps: Pick a consistent bedtime and wake time.
Switch screens off 30–60 minutes before bed.
Dim the lights and keep the room cool and dark.
Try gentle stretching or slow breathing before sleep.
tips: Avoid caffeine in the late afternoon and evening.

items.name: 5-Minute Stress Reset
items.summary: Stress can drive cravings and affect skin — a short breathing break helps.
steps: Sit comfortably and relax your shoulders.
Inhale through your nose for 4 counts.
Exhale slowly for 6 counts.
Repeat for 5 minutes.
tips: Pair it with an existing habit, like after brushing your teeth.

items.name: Weekly Meal Prep Plan
items.summary: Planning ahead makes healthy choices the easy choices on busy days.
steps: Pick 3–4 dinners and 2–3 breakfasts for the week.
Write one grocery list and shop once.
Wash and chop vegetables, cook a grain, and prepare a protein.
Store in portioned containers for the next 3 days.
tips: Keep one flexible meal for eating out.

items.name: Daily Step Goal
items.summary: Everyday movement adds up. Track steps to build momentum.
steps: Check your current average steps for a week.
Add 1,000 steps to that number.
Use stairs, short walks and phone calls on foot to get there.
Increase the goal every 1–2 weeks.
tips: Consistency beats big numbers on occasional days.

items.name: Morning Skin Routine
items.summary: A simple three-step routine is the base of healthy-looking skin.
steps: Cleanse gently with a mild face wash and lukewarm water.
Apply a moisturiser suited to your skin type.
Finish with a broad-spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher.
tips: Pat your face dry rather than rubbing.
Introduce one new product at a time.
items.note: Persistent acne, pigmentation or sensitivity should be assessed — book a consultation rather than self-treating.

items.name: Evening Skin Routine
items.summary: Remove the day's sunscreen and impurities, then let skin repair overnight.
steps: Remove makeup and sunscreen with a gentle cleanser.
Wash your face with lukewarm water and pat dry.
Apply a suitable night moisturiser.
Use any prescribed treatment as directed.
tips: Never sleep with makeup on.
Change your pillowcase weekly.

items.name: Sun Protection Habit
items.summary: Sun exposure is a leading driver of visible skin ageing and pigmentation.
steps: Apply sunscreen 15 minutes before going out — about two finger-lengths for face and neck.
Reapply every 2–3 hours outdoors.
Add a hat, sunglasses and shade during peak sun hours.
tips: Don't forget ears, neck and the back of your hands.

items.name: Gentle Facial Massage
items.summary: A relaxing massage that supports circulation and eases facial tension.
steps: Wash hands and apply a light oil or moisturiser to clean skin.
With fingertips, make small upward and outward strokes from the chin to the ears.
Glide from the nose toward the temples, then from the centre of the forehead outward.
Finish by gently pressing along the jawline.
tips: Use light pressure — never drag or tug the skin.
Skip if you have active acne, infection or irritation.

items.name: Face Relaxation Exercises
items.summary: Gentle facial movements to release jaw, cheek and forehead tension.
steps: Relax your jaw, lips slightly apart, and breathe slowly.
Smile gently with lips closed and hold for 5 seconds, then release.
Raise your eyebrows softly, hold for 3 seconds, then relax.
Massage your jaw hinge in small circles to release clenching.
tips: These help relaxation; they aren't a substitute for professional contouring care.
Stop if you feel pain.
items.note: Interested in contouring or anti-ageing options? A consultation can outline what's suitable for you.

items.name: Neck Posture Chin Tucks
items.summary: Good posture supports the neck and jawline and reduces strain from screen time.
steps: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
Gently draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin.
Hold for 5 seconds, then release.
Repeat 8–10 times.
tips: Keep your eyes level — don't tilt up or down.

items.name: Skin-Friendly Habits
items.summary: Everyday habits that show up on your skin: hydration, sleep, nutrition and touch.
steps: Drink water through the day and eat fruit and vegetables rich in colour.
Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep.
Avoid picking or squeezing spots.
Keep phones and hands clean before touching your face.
tips: Smoking and excess sugar can dull skin and speed up visible ageing.

lifestyle.title: Lifestyle Reset
lifestyle.blurb: Your biggest win is building small, repeatable habits — movement, sleep and stress — before anything complicated. A guided plan helps these stick.
plan: Aim for a daily 20–30 minute walk
Set a consistent sleep and wake time
Add one 5-minute stress reset daily
Review progress after two weeks

nutrition.title: Nutrition-First Slimming
nutrition.blurb: Food choices will make the biggest difference for you. A diet plan that suits your routine and preferences works better than strict rules.
plan: Use the plate method for main meals
Include protein at every meal
Swap sugary drinks and snacks for simpler options
Get a personalised diet plan from your doctor

active.title: Active Body Toning
active.blurb: You're ready for more structured movement. Pair light strength work with good nutrition and regular progress checks for steady results.
plan: 3 short strength sessions a week at home
Daily walking or interval walks
Protein at every meal to support muscle
Track measurements and review every few weeks

skin.title: Glow & Skin Care Routine
skin.blurb: A simple, consistent routine plus the right everyday habits is where healthy-looking skin starts. A doctor can tailor products to your skin type and concerns.
plan: Cleanse, moisturise and use sunscreen daily
Introduce one new product at a time
Prioritise hydration and 7–8 hours of sleep
Get a routine built for your skin type

contour.title: Facial Contour & Anti-Ageing Focus
contour.blurb: Your goals go beyond a routine. A proper assessment of your skin and face lets the doctor suggest what — if anything — is genuinely suitable for you.
plan: Protect skin with daily sunscreen
Support skin with hydration and sleep
Try gentle face relaxation and posture habits
Discuss contouring and anti-ageing options in a consultation
